Abstract: Disclosed herein is a fabrication method and a polymer composite radiation shield designed to provide effective gamma-ray attenuation. The composite comprises a polymer matrix of liquid silicone rubber, reinforced with high atomic number (Z) fillers including tungsten in a fixed concentration and antimony in a varying concentration, to enhance shielding performance across different gamma-ray energy levels. The disclosed fabrication method includes mechanical mixing of the polymer and fillers for a predetermined duration to ensure homogeneous dispersion, followed by vacuum treatment to remove trapped air bubbles, improving material density and shielding efficiency. A polymerization catalyst is introduced to initiate cross-linking and enhance structural integrity. The composite is then cast into a mold of predetermined thickness and subjected to a two-stage curing process, initial curing at room temperature for 24 hours, followed by post-curing in a vacuum oven at 80°C for 8 hours.

Abstract: ABSTRACT Title: Drug Entangled Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotubes Against Breast Cancer The present invention relates to a therapeutic composition containing capsaicin for the treatment of breast cancer. The composition utilizes capsaicin-loaded carboxylate multi-walled carbon nanotubes (FA-CAP-COOHMWCNT) for targeted drug delivery. Molecular docking studies confirmed the binding affinity of capsaicin with breast cancer-related proteins, including Progesterone Receptor (1A28), Estrogen Receptor Alpha (3ERT), and C-Src Kinase (2OIQ). Molecular dynamics simulations conducted for 200 ns to 1000 ns demonstrated the stability of the capsaicin-receptor complexes. The formulation was characterized through FTIR, SEM, TEM, XRD, particle size analysis, and zeta potential measurements, indicating favourable physical and chemical properties. In-vitro cytotoxicity studies on MCF-7 breast cancer cells revealed significant anticancer activity with an IC50 value of 29.97 μg/mL. Preclinical evaluation in a DMBA-induced breast cancer rat model confirmed the formulation's safety and efficacy, with effective tumour size reduction and improved antioxidant activity. This invention offers a novel approach for breast cancer treatment by combining targeted delivery with enhanced therapeutic efficiency.

Abstract: The present invention introduces the "Muco Marker," an innovative instrument designed to enhance the precision and efficiency of free gingival grafting procedures. Free gingival grafting is a widely used technique to increase the zone of attached gingiva and address gingival recession, but challenges in accurately measuring recipient and donor sites often limit its effectiveness. The Muco Marker is a prototype designed and fabricated with a focus on practical functionality. It features four adjustable arms, each 10mm in length, equipped with sharp pointers that can be customized to the required dimensions of the gingival defect. These pointers create precise bleeding points on the donor site to facilitate accurate tissue harvesting. The instrument integrates measurement and marking into a single device, streamlining the grafting process and reducing technique sensitivity. A functional model was carefully developed to ensure precise measurements and ease of use. This innovative tool represents a significant advancement in periodontal aesthetic surgery by enabling clinicians to perform free gingival grafting procedures with greater accuracy, efficiency, and reliability.

Abstract: The invention discloses a Split Ring Resonator (SRR) loaded conformal loop filter designed for S-band applications, featuring dual-band reconfigurability and enhanced performance metrics. The filter incorporates symmetrical tuning stubs, including E-stubs and T-stubs, to achieve reduced insertion loss and improved fractional bandwidth. The integration of SRRs into the ground plane minimizes transmission losses and enhances frequency selectivity. The conformal geometry enables seamless adaptation to non-planar surfaces, ensuring consistent performance across diverse environments. The dual-band functionality is facilitated through reconfiguration using a varactor diode, enabling dynamic adjustment of the second band from 4.2 GHz to 3.9 GHz while maintaining consistent bandwidth. Fabricated on a double-sided FR-4 PCB substrate, the filter demonstrates excellent agreement between simulated and measured results, with a return loss exceeding -10 dB and operational frequencies ranging from 2.05 GHz to 2.25 GHz. This invention addresses the growing need for reconfigurable filters in advanced communication systems, including MIMO, 5G, and multiband wireless devices.

Abstract: Title: In-situ Superporous Hydrogels and Swellable Vaginal Tablet as Cervix Plugs for an Amplified Contraception Potential The present invention describes the development of a biopolymer-based reversible in-situ cervix plug for contraception, utilizing superporous hydrogel hybrids (SPHH) and swellable vaginal tablets (SVT). Chitosan, psyllium, and polycarbophil were used to formulate SPHH through microwave-assisted and lyophilization techniques, with vanillin as a crosslinking agent and zinc acetate as a spermicidal agent. SVT were developed using the wet granulation method, incorporating superporous hydrogels as plug-forming agents along with disintegrants and bioadhesive agents to enhance swelling, adhesion, and cervix plug formation. Characterization studies, including FTIR, DSC, TGA, XRD, and SEM, confirmed the formation of an interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) with high porosity. Box-Behnken Design optimization ensured the selection of formulations with improved mechanical strength, bioadhesion, and controlled swelling properties. Ex-vivo spermicidal studies demonstrated rapid sperm immobilization, with CPYH achieving 100% contraception effectiveness, while CPCH and marketed formulations exhibited 83.33% effectiveness. Turbidimetric analysis confirmed that the formulations support lactobacilli recolonization, maintaining vaginal microbiota balance. In-vivo irritation studies indicated biocompatibility and minimal irritation upon repeated application. Stability testing conducted as per ICH guidelines demonstrated formulation integrity over time. The invention provides a non-hormonal, biodegradable, and user-friendly contraceptive option with effective spermicidal activity and reversibility, addressing the limitations of existing contraceptive methods.

The 2:4 optical decoder, constructed by interconnecting three 1:2 decoders, operates at a wavelength of 1.57 μm and occupies a compact area of 2.935 × 1012 nm2. It ensures low power consumption and efficient signal processing. The optical D flip-flop utilizes MRRs to perform data storage and retrieval at wavelengths of 1.55 μm and 1.4 μm, leveraging the resonance properties of the MRR for fast and reliable operation. Simulations validate the performance of both devices, highlighting their suitability for integration into advanced optical communication and computing systems requiring low power, miniaturized designs, and stable functionality.

Abstract: Aperture arrays-based antennas offer higher gain and wideband operation, with the pyramidal horn being one such antenna that can be applied in array configurations. Traditional approaches use inline or right-angle feed methods to power each element, requiring numerous connectors, which increases cost and complexity. The proposed waveguide slot coupled pyramidal horn array addresses this issue by utilizing a slot coupled waveguide as the feed, which efficiently powers an entire linear array of pyramidal horn antennas. This configuration reduces the need for multiple input feeds, leading to cost-effectiveness and improved gain. Furthermore, by shaping the open-ended waveguide into a pyramidal horn, the gain of the array is enhanced, and the beamwidth is narrowed. This waveguide slot coupled pyramidal horn array configuration also lends itself to planar array designs, where the gain can be further increased to over 16.5 dB with reduced beamwidth. The proposed system finds applications in monopulse radars, space-fed antenna arrays, parabolic reflectors, and beam-steering networks, making it ideal for high-precision communication and radar systems.

This is because the usual steel or elastomeric ligatures are not necessary in self-ligating brackets. It is claimed that passive designs generate even less friction than active ones. With reduced friction and hence less force needed to produce tooth movement, self-ligating brackets are proposed to have the potential advantages of producing more physiologically harmonious tooth movement by not overpowering the musculature and interrupting the periodontal vascular supply.

Abstract: The robot is designed to autonomously navigate crop rows using advanced navigation and sensing technologies while continuously monitoring the field environment. Equipped with vision-based perception and machine-learning algorithms, the WEED FREE BOT accurately distinguishes weeds from crop plants in real time. Upon detection, the system applies targeted weed control actions, including localized herbicide micro-spraying, mechanical removal, or non-chemical thermal treatment, thereby minimizing damage to crops and significantly reducing chemical usage. The robot operates on an energy-efficient power system with intelligent power management to support extended field operations.
